title: Madaniy kontekst va tarixiy ishoralar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida ingliz matnlari va nutqidagi mifologik, diniy, tarixiy, adabiy va media ishoralarni taniysiz, har birining manbasini va asosiy ma’nosini bir gap bilan tushuntirasiz, o‘zgartirilgan ishoralarni sarlavhalarda ilg‘aysiz va besh bosqichli usul bilan notanish ishorani mustaqil talqin qilasiz.

scenes.title: Madaniy ishoralar
board: Cultural Context and Historical References
(madaniy kontekst va tarixiy ishoralar)
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we listened for tone and irony. Today we decode allusions: short references that carry whole stories from myth, history, literature and film.
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum, xush kelibsiz! Oldingi darsda tez nutqda ohang, kinoya va yashirin niyatni ilg‘ashni o‘rgandik. Bugun yana bir yashirin qatlamga o‘tamiz: madaniy va tarixiy ishoralar. Dars oxirida mif, tarix, adabiyot va kinodan olingan ishoralarni taniysiz, ularning manbasini tushuntirasiz va notanish ishorani mustaqil talqin qilasiz.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. Oldingi safar ohang va kinoyani tingladik. Bugun ishoralarni ochamiz: mif, tarix, adabiyot va kinodan butun bir hikoyani olib keladigan qisqa havolalar.

scenes.title: Ishora nima
board: allusion = a short reference to a known story
Sources: myth · Bible · history · literature · media
Two words → a whole story
scenes.say: An allusion is a shortcut. Instead of explaining that a plan contains a hidden danger, a writer simply calls it a Trojan horse and trusts you to know the story.
scenes.say_native: Ishora, inglizcha “allusion”, hammaga tanish deb hisoblangan hikoyaga qisqa havola. Muallif voqeani tushuntirmaydi, faqat ikki-uch so‘z bilan eslatadi va o‘quvchi qolganini o‘zi to‘ldiradi. Siz grammatika va so‘zlarni bilasiz, lekin ishorani tanimasangiz, gapning ma’nosi ochilmaydi. Asosiy manbalar beshta: mif, Injil, tarix, adabiyot va kino-televideniye.
scenes.say_uz: Ishora qisqa yo‘l. Muallif rejada yashirin xavf borligini tushuntirish o‘rniga uni shunchaki Troya oti deb ataydi va hikoyani bilishingizga ishonadi.

scenes.title: Yunon miflari (1)
board: Achilles’ heel = a fatal weakness
Pandora’s box = a source of endless trouble
a Trojan horse = a hidden threat inside a gift

examples.t: The new law could open a Pandora’s box.
examples.uz: Yangi qonun ko‘p muammolar eshigini ochishi mumkin.

scenes.say: Interestingly, Pandora’s box was originally a jar in the Greek sources. And a Trojan horse is now also the name for malicious software that looks harmless.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu: madaniy ishoralar, avvalo yunon miflari. Axillesni onasi tovonidan ushlab muqaddas suvga botirgan, shuning uchun tovoni yagona zaif joyi qolgan: “Achilles’ heel” zaif nuqta. Pandora taqiqlangan idishni ochib, dunyoga barcha balolarni chiqargan: “open Pandora’s box”. Yunonlar Troyaga ichida askarlar yashiringan yog‘och otni sovg‘a qilgan: “a Trojan horse”.
scenes.say_uz: Qizig‘i, yunon manbalarida Pandoraning qutisi aslida ko‘za bo‘lgan. Troya oti esa hozir zararsiz ko‘rinadigan zararli dasturning nomi ham.

scenes.title: Yunon miflari (2)
board: a Herculean task = extremely hard work
a Sisyphean task = endless, futile work
the Midas touch = the ability to make money

examples.t: Cleaning up the city’s finances is a Herculean task.
examples.uz: Shahar moliyasini tartibga solish o‘ta og‘ir vazifa.

scenes.say: Herculean and Sisyphean both describe hard work, but the difference is crucial: a Herculean task can be completed, while a Sisyphean one never ends.
scenes.say_native: Yana uchta mashhur ishora. Gerakl o‘n ikki imkonsiz jasoratni bajargan: “a Herculean task” juda og‘ir, lekin bajarsa bo‘ladigan ish. Sizif esa toshni tog‘ga abadiy dumalatib chiqarishga hukm qilingan, tosh har safar pastga qaytgan: “a Sisyphean task” cheksiz va behuda mehnat. Ikkalasini farqlang. Shoh Midas tekkan narsa oltinga aylangan: “the Midas touch” pul topish qobiliyati.
scenes.say_uz: Herculean va Sisyphean ikkalasi ham og‘ir mehnatni bildiradi, lekin farq muhim: gerakl vazifasini tugatish mumkin, sizif vazifasi esa hech qachon tugamaydi.

scenes.title: Injildan kelgan ishoralar
board: a Good Samaritan = a stranger who helps
David and Goliath = small vs mighty
the prodigal son = one who returns after wasting
the writing on the wall = a sign of coming doom

examples.t: It was a David and Goliath battle between a café and a global chain.
examples.uz: Bu kichik kafe bilan global tarmoq o‘rtasidagi Dovud va Jolut jangi edi.

scenes.say: When a company says the writing was on the wall, it means the signs of failure were obvious long before the end.
scenes.say_native: Ingliz madaniyatida Injil hikoyalari ham keng ishlatiladi, hatto dindor bo‘lmagan odamlar nutqida ham. “A Good Samaritan” notanish odamga beg‘araz yordam beruvchi. “David and Goliath” kichikning ulkan raqib bilan kurashi. “The prodigal son” mol-mulkini sovurib, uyiga qaytgan o‘g‘il. “The writing on the wall” yaqinlashayotgan halokat belgisi.
scenes.say_uz: Kompaniya the writing was on the wall desa, muvaffaqiyatsizlik belgilari oxiridan ancha oldin ko‘rinib turganini bildiradi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek madaniyati bilan qiyos
board: Uzbek: Farhod (huge labour), Majnun (mad with love), Afandi
Shared: Nuh to‘foni = Noah’s flood · Dovud va Jolut = David and Goliath
Same mechanism, different library
scenes.say: Some stories are shared across Islamic and Christian traditions, so David and Goliath or Noah’s Ark may already be familiar to you under slightly different names.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida ham ishoralar bor: og‘ir mehnatni Farhodga, telbalarcha sevgini Majnunga qiyoslaymiz, ayyorona hazilni Afandiga bog‘laymiz. Mexanizm bir xil, faqat kutubxona boshqa. Yaxshi xabar: ba’zi hikoyalar umumiy. Qur’ondagi Dovud va Jolut, Nuh to‘foni, Yusuf qissasi ingliz madaniyatidagi David and Goliath, Noah’s flood bilan bir manbadan. Bu sizga ko‘prik bo‘ladi.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi hikoyalar islom va xristian an’analarida umumiy, shuning uchun Dovud va Jolut yoki Nuh kemasi sizga biroz boshqacha nomlar bilan tanish bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Ishorani buzish
board: ✗ Achilles’ foot · open Pandora’s door
✗ a Herculean task = an endless task
✓ Achilles’ heel · open Pandora’s box
scenes.say: Allusions are fixed. Change a single word and native readers will notice immediately, because the phrase no longer points to the story.
scenes.say_native: Ishoralar qotib qolgan iboralar, ularni o‘zgartirib bo‘lmaydi. “Achilles’ foot” emas, faqat “heel”. “Pandora’s door” emas, “Pandora’s box”. Ma’nosini aralashtirish ham xato: “Herculean” tugaydigan og‘ir ish, cheksiz ish uchun “Sisyphean”. Yana bir nuqta: “Achilles’ heel” ning urg‘usi “a-KIL-eez”, ya’ni ikkinchi bo‘g‘inda.
scenes.say_uz: Ishoralar o‘zgarmas. Bitta so‘zni o‘zgartirsangiz, ingliz o‘quvchisi darhol sezadi, chunki ibora endi hikoyaga ishora qilmaydi.

scenes.title: Ma’nosini tushuntiring
board: 1 The new manager seems to have the Midas touch.
2 Answering emails is a Sisyphean task.
3 A passer-by acted as a Good Samaritan.
4 The free app was a Trojan horse.
scenes.say: Explain each allusion. One: The new manager seems to have the Midas touch. Two: Answering emails is a Sisyphean task. Three: A passer-by acted as a Good Samaritan. Four: The free app was a Trojan horse.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Har biridagi ishorani toping, uning manbasini ayting va gapning ma’nosini o‘z so‘zlaringiz bilan tushuntiring. To‘rtinchi gapga e’tibor bering: bepul ilova nima uchun Troya oti bo‘lishi mumkin? Har bir hikoyaning faqat bitta asosiy xususiyatini eslang, shu kifoya. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir ishorani tushuntiring. Bir: Yangi rahbarda Midas qo‘li borga o‘xshaydi. Ikki: Xatlarga javob berish sizif mehnati. Uch: O‘tkinchi yaxshi samariyalik bo‘ldi. To‘rt: Bepul ilova Troya oti edi.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Everything he does makes money
2 Endless, futile work
3 A stranger helped
4 It hid something harmful
scenes.say: Notice that these allusions work as ordinary vocabulary. You do not need to retell the myth; you only need to know the one feature of the story that the phrase points to.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: Midas, yunon mifi, rahbar nimaga qo‘l ursa, foyda keltiradi. Ikkinchi: Sizif, javob berganingiz sari yangi xatlar keladi, ish hech tugamaydi. Uchinchi: Injil, notanish odam beg‘araz yordam berdi. To‘rtinchi: Troya oti, bepul ilova ichida zararli dastur yoki ma’lumot yig‘ish yashiringan edi.
scenes.say_uz: Bu ishoralar oddiy so‘z kabi ishlashiga e’tibor bering. Mifni qayta aytib berish shart emas, faqat ibora ishora qilayotgan hikoyaning bitta xususiyatini bilish kifoya.

scenes.title: Qadimgi tarix
board: cross the Rubicon = take an irreversible step
a Pyrrhic victory = a win that costs too much
fiddle while Rome burns = ignore a crisis

examples.t: By resigning publicly, she had crossed the Rubicon.
examples.uz: Ochiq iste’fo berib, u ortga yo‘l qoldirmadi.

scenes.say: According to legend, the emperor Nero played music while Rome burned in the year sixty-four. Historians doubt the story, but the phrase survives: to fiddle while Rome burns.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: tez-tez tilga olinadigan tarixiy voqealar. Miloddan avvalgi 49-yilda Yuliy Sezar Rubikon daryosidan qo‘shini bilan o‘tib, Rimga qarshi fuqarolar urushini boshlagan: “cross the Rubicon” ortga qaytmaydigan qadam. Shoh Pirr miloddan avvalgi III asrda rimliklarni yenggan, lekin shunchalik ko‘p askar yo‘qotganki, g‘alaba mag‘lubiyatga teng bo‘lgan: “a Pyrrhic victory”.
scenes.say_uz: Rivoyatga ko‘ra, imperator Neron oltmish to‘rtinchi yilda Rim yonayotganda musiqa chalgan. Tarixchilar bunga shubha qiladi, lekin ibora saqlanib qolgan: Rim yonayotganda skripka chalmoq.

scenes.title: Yangi tarix
board: meet your Waterloo = a final, decisive defeat (1815)
the Iron Curtain = the Cold War divide (Churchill, 1946)
the Dunkirk spirit = courage in a crisis (1940)

examples.t: The champion finally met his Waterloo in the semi-final.
examples.uz: Chempion nihoyat yarim finalda hal qiluvchi mag‘lubiyatga uchradi.

scenes.say: British speakers in particular refer to the Second World War: the Dunkirk spirit and the Blitz spirit both describe calm, collective resilience under pressure.
scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida yangi tarixdan ham ko‘p ishora bor. Napoleon 1815-yilda Vaterloo jangida yakuniy mag‘lubiyatga uchragan: “meet your Waterloo”. Cherchill 1946-yilda Yevropani bo‘lgan “temir parda” haqida gapirgan: “the Iron Curtain”. 1940-yilda Dyunkerkdan qo‘shinlarni evakuatsiya qilishda oddiy qayiqlar ham qatnashgan: “the Dunkirk spirit” qiyinchilikda birlashish ruhi.
scenes.say_uz: Ayniqsa britaniyaliklar Ikkinchi jahon urushiga ko‘p ishora qiladi: Dunkirk spirit va Blitz spirit ikkalasi ham bosim ostida xotirjam, birgalikdagi chidamlilikni bildiradi.

scenes.title: Jurnalistika ishoralari
board: -gate (Watergate, 1972–74) = a scandal
a witch hunt (Salem, 1692) = unfair persecution
a Luddite (1811–16) = someone who resists technology

examples.t: My dad is a bit of a Luddite: he still refuses to use a smartphone.
examples.uz: Dadam biroz texnologiya dushmani: hali ham smartfondan voz kechadi.

scenes.say: The suffix gate is now fully productive in English: journalists attach it to almost any word to label a new scandal, often with a touch of irony.
scenes.say_native: Yangiliklarda ko‘p uchraydigan uchta ishora. 1972-yilgi Uotergeyt mojarosi prezident Niksonning 1974-yildagi iste’fosiga olib kelgan, shundan beri har qanday janjal nomiga “-gate” qo‘shiladi. 1692-yilgi Salem sud jarayonlaridan “a witch hunt”, adolatsiz ta’qib. 1811–1816 yillarda mashinalarni sindirgan to‘quvchilardan “a Luddite”, yangi texnologiyaga qarshi odam.
scenes.say_uz: Gate qo‘shimchasi hozir ingliz tilida to‘liq unumli: jurnalistlar uni yangi janjalni nomlash uchun deyarli har qanday so‘zga, ko‘pincha kinoya bilan qo‘shadi.

scenes.title: Koinot davri iboralari
board: ‘one small step…’ (Armstrong, 1969)
‘Houston, we have a problem’ (Apollo 13, 1970)
original: ‘Houston, we’ve had a problem.’

examples.t: Houston, we have a problem: the printer’s out of ink again.
examples.uz: Xyuston, bizda muammo bor: printerda yana siyoh tugadi.

scenes.say: Popular memory often changes famous quotations. The crew actually said we’ve had a problem, but the film version, we have a problem, is the one everyone quotes.
scenes.say_native: Kosmos tarixidan ikki ibora. 1969-yilda Armstrong Oyga qadam qo‘yib, “one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind” degan. Bu iborani kichik, lekin tarixiy qadamlar haqida hazil bilan ishlatishadi. 1970-yilda Apollon 13 ekipaji “Houston, we’ve had a problem” degan, ommaviy shakli esa “Houston, we have a problem”. Bugun u kichik muammoni hazil bilan e’lon qilishda ishlatiladi.
scenes.say_uz: Ommaviy xotira mashhur iqtiboslarni ko‘pincha o‘zgartiradi. Ekipaj aslida we’ve had a problem degan, lekin hamma kinodagi we have a problem shaklini iqtibos qiladi.

scenes.title: O‘zbek tarixiy xotirasi bilan qiyos
board: Uzbek references: Buyuk Ipak yo‘li, Ulug‘bek, Temur
British references: Waterloo, Dunkirk, the Blitz
Explain your own allusions to foreigners
scenes.say: A reference that feels obvious inside one culture can be completely opaque outside it. Skilled communicators notice this and add a brief explanation when they cross a cultural border.
scenes.say_native: Har bir xalqning tarixiy xotirasi o‘z ishoralarini yaratadi. Biz “Ulug‘bek rasadxonasi” yoki “Buyuk Ipak yo‘li” deganda butun bir davrni eslaymiz, britaniyalik o‘quvchi esa buni bilmasligi mumkin. Xuddi shunday, ingliz uchun “Dunkirk” bir so‘zda butun bir milliy kayfiyat. Ikki tomonlama xulosa: inglizcha ishoralarni o‘rganing va o‘zbekcha ishoralaringizni chet ellik uchun tushuntira bilish ham C2 ko‘nikmasi.
scenes.say_uz: Bir madaniyat ichida aniq tuyulgan ishora uning tashqarisida butunlay tushunarsiz bo‘lishi mumkin. Mohir suhbatdosh buni sezadi va madaniy chegarani kesib o‘tganda qisqa izoh qo‘shadi.

scenes.title: Ma’noni teskari tushunish
board: ✗ a Pyrrhic victory = a great victory
✓ a victory that cost almost everything
✗ meet your Waterloo = succeed  ✓ = be finally defeated
scenes.say: If you are not sure whether an allusion is positive or negative, check the original story. The ending of the story almost always decides the meaning of the phrase.
scenes.say_native: Tarixiy ishoralarda keng uchraydigan xato: ma’noni teskari tushunish. “Pyrrhic victory” buyuk g‘alaba emas, juda qimmatga tushgan g‘alaba. “Meet your Waterloo” muvaffaqiyat emas, hal qiluvchi mag‘lubiyat, chunki Napoleon u yerda yengilgan. “Witch hunt” haqiqiy jinoyatchini qidirish emas, adolatsiz ta’qib. Notanish ishorani taxmin qilib ishlatishdan oldin manbasini tekshiring.
scenes.say_uz: Ishora ijobiymi yoki salbiymi, ishonchingiz komil bo‘lmasa, asl hikoyani tekshiring. Hikoyaning yakuni deyarli har doim iboraning ma’nosini belgilaydi.

scenes.title: Tarixiy ishoralar
board: 1 The team won, but lost three key players. A ___ victory.
2 Once the contract was signed, there was no going back: they had crossed the ___.
3 The press called the expenses scandal ‘Receiptgate’. Origin?
4 He calls anyone who criticises him a ‘witch hunt’. Meaning?
scenes.say: One: The team won, but lost three key players. A blank victory. Two: Once the contract was signed, they had crossed the blank. Three: Where does gate in Receiptgate come from? Four: What does he mean by a witch hunt?
scenes.say_native: To‘rt topshiriq. Birinchi va ikkinchida bo‘sh joyni to‘ldiring. Uchinchida “-gate” qo‘shimchasining kelib chiqishini ayting. To‘rtinchida “witch hunt” bu kontekstda nimani anglatishini va so‘zlovchining munosabati qanday ekanini tushuntiring. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Jamoa yutdi, lekin uch asosiy o‘yinchisini yo‘qotdi. Qanday g‘alaba? Ikki: Shartnoma imzolangach, ular nimadan o‘tgan edi? Uch: Receiptgate dagi gate qayerdan kelgan? To‘rt: Witch hunt deganda u nimani nazarda tutadi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Pyrrhic
2 Rubicon
3 Watergate (1972–74)
4 Unfair persecution (his claim)
scenes.say: Allusions are rarely neutral. Calling an investigation a witch hunt is not a description; it is an accusation, and a careful listener notices whose story is being told.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: “a Pyrrhic victory”, g‘alaba juda qimmatga tushdi. Ikkinchi: “crossed the Rubicon”, ortga yo‘l yo‘q. Uchinchi: Uotergeyt mojarosidan, “-gate” janjalni bildiradi. To‘rtinchi: u o‘zini adolatsiz ta’qib qurboni deb ko‘rsatmoqda. E’tibor bering, bu so‘zlovchining da’vosi, fakt emas. Ishora ko‘pincha so‘zlovchining pozitsiyasini ham ochadi.
scenes.say_uz: Ishoralar kamdan-kam betaraf bo‘ladi. Tergovni witch hunt deb atash tavsif emas, ayblov, ziyrak tinglovchi esa kimning hikoyasi aytilayotganini payqaydi.

scenes.title: Shekspir
board: star-crossed lovers (Romeo and Juliet)
the green-eyed monster = jealousy (Othello)
All that glisters is not gold (The Merchant of Venice)
To be or not to be (Hamlet)
scenes.say: Shakespeare’s lines are so embedded in English that many speakers quote him without realising it. All that glitters is not gold is the modern form of his original glisters.
scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: adabiyot va media. Shekspir ingliz tiliga yuzlab ibora bergan. “Star-crossed lovers” taqdir qarshi bo‘lgan oshiqlar, “Romeo va Julyetta” dan. “The green-eyed monster”, ya’ni yashil ko‘zli maxluq, rashk, “Otello” dan. “All that glisters is not gold” “Venetsiya savdogari” dan, bugun odatda “glitters” shaklida aytiladi. “To be or not to be” esa “Gamlet” dan, ko‘pincha sarlavhalarda o‘zgartiriladi.
scenes.say_uz: Shekspir satrlari ingliz tiliga shunchalik singganki, ko‘p odamlar uni bilmagan holda iqtibos qiladi. All that glitters is not gold uning asl glisters shaklining zamonaviy ko‘rinishi.

scenes.title: Romanlardan sifatlar
board: Orwellian / Big Brother (1984, published 1949)
Kafkaesque = absurd, nightmarish bureaucracy
Dickensian = grim Victorian poverty
a Scrooge = a mean person · Jekyll and Hyde

examples.t: Getting a visa was a Kafkaesque experience.
examples.uz: Viza olish kafkacha, ya’ni bema’ni byurokratik azob edi.

scenes.say: Describing a tax office as Kafkaesque tells the reader far more than calling it confusing: it suggests endless forms, contradictory rules and no one to blame.
scenes.say_native: Ba’zi yozuvchilar nomi sifatga aylangan. “Orwellian” Oruellning “1984” romanidan, davlat hammani kuzatadigan totalitar nazorat; “Big Brother” ham shu yerdan. “Kafkaesque” Kafka asarlaridagidek bema’ni va chiqib bo‘lmaydigan byurokratiya. “Dickensian” Dikkens tasvirlagan og‘ir qashshoqlik. “A Scrooge” xasis odam. “Jekyll and Hyde” ikki xil, yaxshi va yomon qiyofali shaxs.
scenes.say_uz: Soliq idorasini Kafkaesque deb atash uni chalkash deyishdan ko‘ra ko‘proq narsani aytadi: cheksiz blankalar, bir-biriga zid qoidalar va aybdor yo‘qligini bildiradi.

scenes.title: Ertak va bolalar adabiyoti
board: the emperor’s new clothes = a truth nobody dares say
down the rabbit hole = into a strange, absorbing world
a Cinderella story = from obscurity to success

examples.t: I clicked one link and went down a rabbit hole for three hours.
examples.uz: Bitta havolani bosib, uch soat qiziq olamga sho‘ng‘ib ketdim.

scenes.say: Down the rabbit hole is now everyday internet language: it describes losing hours to one fascinating topic after another.
scenes.say_native: Ertaklar ham ishoralarga boy. Andersenning “Qirolning yangi libosi” ertagida hamma ko‘rib turgan haqiqatni faqat bir bola aytadi: “the emperor’s new clothes” hamma ko‘rsa ham aytishga jur’at etmaydigan haqiqat. Lyuis Kerrollning “Alisa” sidan “down the rabbit hole”, g‘alati va qiziq olamga sho‘ng‘ib ketish. “A Cinderella story” noma’lumlikdan to‘satdan muvaffaqiyatga erishish.
scenes.say_uz: Down the rabbit hole hozir kundalik internet tili: bir qiziq mavzudan boshqasiga o‘tib, soatlarni yo‘qotishni bildiradi.

scenes.title: Kino va televideniye
board: Groundhog Day (1993) = the same day again and again
jump the shark (Happy Days, 1977) = decline after a gimmick
the red pill (The Matrix, 1999) = choosing a hard truth
scenes.say: Media allusions age faster than classical ones. Everyone still understands Groundhog Day, but newer references may be lost on older listeners, and vice versa.
scenes.say_native: Kino va seriallar ham ishora manbai. 1993-yilgi “Groundhog Day” filmida qahramon bir kunni qayta-qayta yashaydi: zerikarli takror. “Jump the shark” 1977-yilgi “Happy Days” serialidagi qahramon akula ustidan suv changisida sakragan epizoddan, ya’ni seriyani saqlab qolish uchun g‘alati hiyla va pasayish boshlanishi. “The red pill” “Matritsa” filmidan, og‘ir haqiqatni tanlash.
scenes.say_uz: Media ishoralari klassik ishoralardan tezroq eskiradi. Groundhog Day ni hali hamma tushunadi, lekin yangiroq ishoralarni keksa tinglovchilar tushunmasligi mumkin, va aksincha.

scenes.title: Frankenstein va Catch-22
board: ✗ Frankenstein = the monster
✓ Frankenstein = the scientist; Frankenstein’s monster
✗ Catch-22 = any problem  ✓ = a circular, no-win rule
scenes.say: In Catch-22, a pilot can be excused from flying if he is insane, but asking to be excused proves he is sane. That circularity is the whole meaning of the phrase.
scenes.say_native: Ikki mashhur xato. Meri Shellining 1818-yilgi romanida Frankenstein maxluq emas, uni yaratgan olim Viktor Frankenstein. Maxluq “Frankenstein’s monster”. Ingliz tilida ham ko‘pchilik buni aralashtiradi, lekin C2 darajasida aniq bo‘ling. Ikkinchisi “Catch-22”: Xellerning 1961-yilgi romanidan, oddiy muammo emas, qoidalar o‘zini o‘zi inkor qilib, chiqish yo‘li qolmagan berk vaziyat.
scenes.say_uz: Catch-22 da uchuvchi aqldan ozgan bo‘lsa, parvozdan ozod qilinadi, lekin ozod qilishni so‘rashning o‘zi uning aqli joyida ekanini isbotlaydi. Iboraning butun ma’nosi shu aylanma mantiqda.

scenes.title: Manba va ma’no
board: 1 Every Monday feels like Groundhog Day.
2 You need experience to get a job, and a job to get experience.
3 The new surveillance law is frankly Orwellian.
4 Nobody dared to say the project had failed: the emperor’s new clothes.
scenes.say: One: Every Monday feels like Groundhog Day. Two: You need experience to get a job, and a job to get experience. Which allusion fits? Three: The new surveillance law is frankly Orwellian. Four: Nobody dared to say the project had failed.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Birinchi, uchinchi va to‘rtinchida ishoraning manbasini va ma’nosini ayting. Ikkinchi gapda ishora so‘zi yo‘q: bu vaziyatni qaysi ishora bilan atash mumkin? Bu teskari yo‘nalishdagi mashq, ya’ni vaziyatdan ishoraga borasiz. Shoshilmang, o‘ylab, javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Har dushanba Groundhog Day ga o‘xshaydi. Ikki: Ishga kirish uchun tajriba, tajriba uchun ish kerak. Qaysi ishora mos? Uch: Yangi kuzatuv qonuni ochig‘i Oruellcha. To‘rt: Loyiha muvaffaqiyatsiz bo‘lganini hech kim aytishga jur’at etmadi.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Film (1993): the same day repeats
2 Catch-22
3 Novel 1984: state surveillance
4 Andersen: a truth no one admits
scenes.say: Moving from a situation to the right allusion is harder than recognising one. It is also the skill that makes your own English sound genuinely native.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: 1993-yilgi film, har dushanba bir xil takrorlanadi. Ikkinchi: bu klassik “Catch-22”, aylanma va chiqishsiz qoida. Uchinchi: Oruellning “1984” romani, davlatning ortiqcha kuzatuvi. To‘rtinchi: Andersen ertagi, hamma biladigan, lekin hech kim aytmaydigan haqiqat. Ikkinchi topshiriq eng qiyini edi, chunki vaziyatdan ishoraga borish kerak edi.
scenes.say_uz: Vaziyatdan to‘g‘ri ishoraga o‘tish ishorani tanishdan qiyinroq. Bu sizning ingliz tilingizni haqiqatan tabiiy qiladigan ko‘nikma ham.

scenes.title: Ishorani talqin qilish: 5 qadam
board: 1 Notice: a capital letter or an odd phrase
2 Identify the source · 3 Recall its key feature
4 Map it onto the situation
5 Read the tone: admiring, ironic, critical?
scenes.say: An unexpected capital letter is often your first clue. When a sentence about a bank suddenly mentions Icarus, you can be fairly sure someone flew too close to the sun.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: notanish ishorani talqin qilish. Besh qadam. Birinchi: payqang, gap o‘rtasida bosh harfli ism yoki kontekstga to‘g‘ri kelmaydigan ibora. Ikkinchi: manbani aniqlang, kerak bo‘lsa qidiring. Uchinchi: hikoyaning bitta asosiy xususiyatini eslang. To‘rtinchi: uni hozirgi vaziyatga ko‘chiring. Beshinchi: ohangni o‘qing, ishora maqtaydimi, kinoya qiladimi yoki tanqid qiladimi.
scenes.say_uz: Kutilmagan bosh harf ko‘pincha birinchi ishora. Bank haqidagi gapda to‘satdan Ikar tilga olinsa, kimdir quyoshga juda yaqin uchganiga deyarli ishonch hosil qilishingiz mumkin.

scenes.title: O‘zgartirilgan ishoralar
board: To tweet or not to tweet? (← To be or not to be)
A Pyrrhic victory for the government
Partygate (← Watergate)

examples.t: To stream or not to stream: the cinema’s dilemma.
examples.uz: Striming qilishmi yoki qilmaslik: kinoteatrning dilemmasi.

scenes.say: Headline writers love to bend a famous phrase. The pleasure for the reader lies in recognising the original under the new words.
scenes.say_native: Jurnalistlar ishoralarni ko‘pincha o‘zgartiradi, ayniqsa sarlavhalarda. “To be or not to be” “To tweet or not to tweet” ga aylanadi. “Watergate” dan “Partygate” kabi yangi so‘zlar yasaladi. O‘zgartirilgan ishorani tanish uchun asl shaklni bilish shart: aks holda sarlavhadagi so‘z o‘yini ko‘rinmay qoladi. Bunday so‘z o‘yini ko‘pincha kinoya bilan birga keladi.
scenes.say_uz: Sarlavha mualliflari mashhur iborani egishni yaxshi ko‘radi. O‘quvchining zavqi yangi so‘zlar ostidan asl iborani tanib olishda.

scenes.title: Talaffuz
board: Achilles /əˈkɪliːz/ · Pyrrhic /ˈpɪrɪk/
Kafkaesque /ˌkæfkəˈesk/ · Orwellian /ɔːˈweliən/
Sisyphean /ˌsɪsɪˈfiːən/ · Herculean /ˌhɜːkjuˈliːən/
scenes.say: Achilles. Pyrrhic. Kafkaesque. Orwellian. Sisyphean. Herculean. Repeat each one after me, and notice how the suffix esque always takes the stress.
scenes.say_native: Ishoralarni to‘g‘ri talaffuz qilish ham muhim, aks holda tinglovchi tanimaydi. “Achilles” da urg‘u ikkinchi bo‘g‘inda: a-KIL-eez, oxiri “z”. “Pyrrhic” ikki bo‘g‘in: PIR-ik. “Kafkaesque” da urg‘u oxirgi bo‘g‘inda: kaf-ka-ESK. “Orwellian” da ikkinchi bo‘g‘inda. “Sisyphean” va “Herculean” da urg‘u “-ean” qo‘shimchasiga, ya’ni “i:” tovushiga tushadi. Ularni ovoz chiqarib takrorlang.
scenes.say_uz: Achilles. Pyrrhic. Kafkaesque. Orwellian. Sisyphean. Herculean. Har birini ortimdan takrorlang va esque qo‘shimchasi har doim urg‘u olishiga e’tibor bering.

scenes.title: Artikllar va ishoralar
board: a Trojan horse · a Herculean task · a Scrooge
the Midas touch · the writing on the wall
his Achilles’ heel · Ø Groundhog Day
scenes.say: Learn each allusion with its article, as a complete chunk. Saying a Midas touch or the Trojan horse in the wrong context immediately sounds foreign.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida artikl yo‘qligi sababli ishoralarda ham xato chiqadi. Ko‘p ishora sanaladigan ot kabi ishlaydi va “a” oladi: “a Trojan horse”, “a Herculean task”, “a Scrooge”. Ba’zilari esa qotib qolgan “the” bilan keladi: “the Midas touch”, “the writing on the wall”. “Achilles’ heel” odatda egalik so‘zi bilan: “his Achilles’ heel”. Film nomi esa artiklsiz: “It’s like Groundhog Day”.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir ishorani artikli bilan, butun blok sifatida o‘rganing. Noto‘g‘ri kontekstda a Midas touch yoki the Trojan horse deyish darhol begona eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Ishoralarni haddan oshirish
board: ✗ This Trojan horse opened Pandora’s box at our Waterloo.
✓ One well-chosen allusion per paragraph
(mixed metaphors = confusion)
scenes.say: One allusion illuminates; three in a row become a joke. Choose the single reference that fits the situation best and let it do its work.
scenes.say_native: Ishoralarni o‘rgangach, ularni ko‘p ishlatish vasvasasi tug‘iladi. “This Trojan horse opened Pandora’s box at our Waterloo” kulgili eshitiladi, chunki uch xil hikoya bir-biriga aralashib ketgan. Inglizlar buni “mixed metaphor” deydi. Yozuvda bitta xatboshiga bitta yaxshi tanlangan ishora yetarli. Akademik esseda esa ulardan juda ehtiyotkor foydalaning.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta ishora yoritadi, ketma-ket uchtasi hazilga aylanadi. Vaziyatga eng mos keladigan bitta ishorani tanlang va uni ishlashga qo‘ying.

scenes.title: Yangilik matnini talqin qiling
board: The minister’s reforms have become a Sisyphean struggle.
Critics say the new app is a Trojan horse for data collection,
and with rivals closing in, the writing may be on the wall.
For her party, it could be a Pyrrhic victory.
scenes.say: The minister’s reforms have become a Sisyphean struggle. Critics say the new app is a Trojan horse for data collection, and with rivals closing in, the writing may be on the wall. For her party, it could be a Pyrrhic victory.
scenes.say_native: Qisqa yangilik matnida to‘rtta ishora bor. Besh qadamli usulni qo‘llang: har bir ishorani toping, manbasini ayting, asosiy ma’nosini va muallifning ohangini aniqlang. Matnning umumiy kayfiyati qanday: optimistikmi yoki xavotirlimi? Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Vazir islohotlari sizif kurashiga aylandi. Tanqidchilar yangi ilovani ma’lumot yig‘ish uchun Troya oti deyishmoqda va raqiblar yaqinlashar ekan, halokat belgilari ko‘rinib turgan bo‘lishi mumkin. Uning partiyasi uchun bu qimmatga tushgan g‘alaba bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Sisyphean (myth): endless, futile effort
Trojan horse (myth): hidden purpose
writing on the wall (Bible): coming failure
Pyrrhic (history): costly win → tone: pessimistic
scenes.say: Every allusion here points the same way, towards failure. Recognising the pattern lets you identify the writer’s stance even before you reach the conclusion.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. “Sisyphean”, yunon mifi: islohotlar tugamaydi va natija bermaydi. “Trojan horse”, mif: ilova ostida yashirin maqsad bor. “The writing on the wall”, Injil: muvaffaqiyatsizlik belgilari. “Pyrrhic victory”, tarix: g‘alaba juda qimmatga tushadi. Umumiy ohang pessimistik va tanqidiy. To‘rtta ishora bitta matnda bo‘lsa ham, har biri alohida gapda.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerdagi har bir ishora bir tomonga, muvaffaqiyatsizlikka qaraydi. Bu qolipni tanish muallif pozitsiyasini xulosaga yetmasdan oldin aniqlash imkonini beradi.

scenes.title: Dialog: ishxonada
board: Ben: … IT won’t give me one until I’ve logged in.
Lola: A proper Catch-22.
… a Pandora’s box of security issues.
scenes.say: Lola: How’s the new system going? Ben: Don’t ask. To get access, I need a password from IT, but IT won’t give me one until I’ve logged in. Lola: A proper Catch-22. Ben: Exactly. And moving ten years of data across is a Herculean task. Lola: Couldn’t you just keep the old system? Ben: We suggested that. Apparently, it would open a Pandora’s box of security issues.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Hamkasblar Lola va Ben yangi kompyuter tizimi haqida gaplashadi. Ben uchta ishora ishlatadi yoki eshitadi. Har bir ishora vaziyatning qaysi tomonini ta’riflayotganiga va Benning so‘nggi gapdagi “apparently” so‘zi orqali bildirgan munosabatiga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say_uz: Lola: Yangi tizim qanday ketyapti? Ben: So‘rama. Kirish uchun IT bo‘limidan parol kerak, lekin ular men tizimga kirmagunimcha parol bermaydi. Lola: Haqiqiy Catch-22. Ben: Aynan. O‘n yillik ma’lumotni ko‘chirish esa gerakl mehnati. Lola: Eski tizimni qoldirib bo‘lmaydimi? Ben: Taklif qildik. Aytishlaricha, bu xavfsizlik muammolarining Pandora qutisini ochar ekan.

scenes.title: Tushunganingizni tekshiring
board: 1 Why is Ben’s situation a Catch-22?
2 What does ‘Herculean’ say about the data move?
3 What is Ben’s attitude to the security argument?
scenes.say: One: why is Ben’s situation a Catch-22? Two: what does Herculean tell you about moving the data? Three: what is Ben’s attitude to the security argument?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: Benning vaziyati nima uchun Catch-22? Ikkinchi: “Herculean” ma’lumot ko‘chirish haqida nimani aytadi, u tugaydimi? Uchinchi: Ben xavfsizlik dalilini qanday qabul qiladi? Oldingi darsdagi “apparently” so‘zining ma’nosini eslang, u bu yerda kalit.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Benning vaziyati nega Catch-22? Ikki: Herculean ma’lumot ko‘chirish haqida nima deydi? Uch: Ben xavfsizlik dalilini qanday qabul qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Each condition depends on the other
2 Very hard but possible
3 Sceptical: ‘Apparently…’
scenes.say: The password depends on logging in, and logging in depends on the password. The data move is hard but finite. And Ben clearly doubts the security argument.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: parol uchun tizimga kirish kerak, tizimga kirish uchun parol kerak, aylanma va chiqishsiz qoida. Ikkinchi: “Herculean” juda og‘ir, lekin bajarsa bo‘ladigan ish, “Sisyphean” emas. Uchinchi: Ben shubhali. “Apparently” bu gapni boshqalar aytgani, o‘zi esa unchalik ishonmasligini bildiradi. Ishora va ohang birgalikda ishlaydi.
scenes.say_uz: Parol tizimga kirishga, kirish esa parolga bog‘liq. Ma’lumot ko‘chirish og‘ir, lekin tugaydigan ish. Ben esa xavfsizlik dalilga aniq shubha qiladi.

scenes.title: Dialog: yangiliklar haqida
board: Amir: A Pyrrhic victory, then.
Amir: Very Orwellian.
Sophie: It’s like Groundhog Day.
scenes.say: Amir: Did you see the election result? Sophie: They won, but they lost forty seats doing it. Amir: A Pyrrhic victory, then. Sophie: Pretty much. And now they want cameras on every street corner. Amir: Very Orwellian. Sophie: And it’s the same debate every single year. It’s like Groundhog Day. Amir: Well, maybe this will be their Waterloo.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Amir va Sofi saylov natijalarini muhokama qiladi. To‘rtta ishora bor: tarixdan, adabiyotdan, kinodan va yana tarixdan. Har biri vaziyatning qaysi tomonini ta’riflashini kuzating. Oxirgi gapda Amir kelajak haqida taxmin qiladi, uning taxminini ishoradan topishingiz kerak.
scenes.say_uz: Amir: Saylov natijasini ko‘rdingmi? Sofi: Yutishdi, lekin buning uchun qirqta o‘rindiqni yo‘qotishdi. Amir: Demak, Pirr g‘alabasi. Sofi: Deyarli shunday. Endi esa har bir ko‘cha burchagiga kamera o‘rnatmoqchi. Amir: Juda Oruellcha. Sofi: Har yili bir xil munozara. Xuddi Groundhog Day. Amir: Balki bu ularning Vaterloosi bo‘lar.

scenes.title: Tushunganingizni tekshiring
board: 1 Why is the win ‘Pyrrhic’?
2 What does ‘Orwellian’ suggest about the cameras?
3 What is ‘like Groundhog Day’?
4 What does Amir predict?
scenes.say: One: why is the win Pyrrhic? Two: what does Orwellian suggest? Three: what is like Groundhog Day? Four: what does Amir predict?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Birinchi: g‘alaba nega Pirr g‘alabasi? Ikkinchi: “Orwellian” kameralar haqida nimani bildiradi? Uchinchi: nima Groundhog Day ga o‘xshaydi? To‘rtinchi: Amir “Waterloo” orqali qanday taxmin qiladi? Har bir javobda ishoraning manbasini ham ayting.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: g‘alaba nega Pirr g‘alabasi? Ikki: Orwellian nimani bildiradi? Uch: nima Groundhog Day ga o‘xshaydi? To‘rt: Amir nimani taxmin qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 They won but lost forty seats
2 Excessive state surveillance (1984)
3 The same debate every year (1993 film)
4 A final, decisive defeat
scenes.say: Four allusions, four sources, and not one of them explained. That is how educated speakers talk, and now you can follow them.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: partiya yutdi, lekin qirqta o‘rindiq yo‘qotdi, g‘alaba qimmatga tushdi. Ikkinchi: “Orwellian”, “1984” romanidan, davlatning ortiqcha kuzatuvi, so‘zlovchi buni tanqid qilyapti. Uchinchi: har yili takrorlanadigan bir xil munozara. To‘rtinchi: Amir bu partiya keyingi safar hal qiluvchi mag‘lubiyatga uchrashi mumkin deb o‘ylaydi.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta ishora, to‘rtta manba va birortasi ham tushuntirilmadi. Bilimli odamlar shunday gapiradi, endi siz ularni tushuna olasiz.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq
board: A Explain 3 allusions in your own words: Achilles’ heel · Catch-22 · Kafkaesque
B Explain one Uzbek allusion (e.g. Farhod) to an English speaker
C Use one English allusion about your own life
scenes.say: Your turn. Explain Achilles’ heel, Catch-22 and Kafkaesque in your own words. Then explain one Uzbek allusion to an English speaker, and use one English allusion about your own life.
scenes.say_native: Endi o‘zingiz gapirasiz yoki yozasiz. Birinchi: “Achilles’ heel”, “Catch-22” va “Kafkaesque” ni o‘z so‘zlaringiz bilan, manbasi bilan tushuntiring. Ikkinchi: bitta o‘zbekcha ishorani, masalan, Farhodni ingliz tilida chet ellikka tushuntiring. Uchinchi: o‘z hayotingiz haqida bitta inglizcha ishorali gap tuzing. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Achilles’ heel, Catch-22 va Kafkaesque ni o‘z so‘zlaringiz bilan tushuntiring. Keyin bitta o‘zbekcha ishorani chet ellikka tushuntiring va o‘z hayotingiz haqida bitta inglizcha ishora ishlating.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javob
board: Farhod: a hero who dug through a mountain for love
→ ‘a labour worthy of Farhod’
My Achilles’ heel is public speaking.
scenes.say: In Uzbek, we compare exhausting work to Farhod, the hero of a poem by Navoi who dug through a mountain to win Shirin. It is a bit like a Herculean task, but with love as the motive. As for me, my Achilles’ heel is public speaking.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javobni tinglang. E’tibor bering, o‘zbekcha ishorani tushuntirganda avval kim ekanini, keyin hikoyaning asosiy xususiyatini va nihoyat bugungi ma’nosini aytamiz. Bu xuddi besh qadamli usulning teskarisi. O‘z javobingizni solishtiring: manba, asosiy xususiyat va ma’no bormi?
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek tilida charchatadigan mehnatni Navoiy dostoni qahramoni Farhodga qiyoslaymiz, u Shirinni deb tog‘ni qazigan. Bu biroz gerakl mehnatiga o‘xshaydi, faqat sabab sevgi. Menga kelsak, mening zaif nuqtam ommaviy nutq.

scenes.title: Takrorlash
board: Myth & Bible: Achilles’ heel, Pandora’s box, David and Goliath
History: Rubicon, Pyrrhic, Waterloo, -gate
Literature & media: Orwellian, Catch-22, Groundhog Day
Interpret: notice → source → feature → map → tone
scenes.say: Notice the reference, find its source, recall the key feature, map it onto the situation and read the tone. That is how a two-word allusion unlocks a whole story.
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Ishora butun hikoyani ikki-uch so‘zga sig‘diradi. Mif va Injildan zaif nuqta, ko‘p muammo va kichikning kurashi haqidagi iboralarni bildik. Tarixdan ortga qaytmaydigan qadam, qimmat g‘alaba va hal qiluvchi mag‘lubiyat. Adabiyot va kinodan Oruell, Kafka, Catch-22 va Groundhog Day. Notanish ishorani besh qadamda talqin qilamiz.
scenes.say_uz: Ishorani payqang, manbasini toping, asosiy xususiyatini eslang, vaziyatga ko‘chiring va ohangni o‘qing. Ikki so‘zlik ishora butun hikoyani shunday ochadi.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Homework: explain 5 cultural references
from authentic texts (news, headlines, podcasts, series)
source + original story + meaning here
scenes.say: Your homework: find and explain five cultural references from authentic texts. Next time we study word formation with prefixes and suffixes.
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: haqiqiy ingliz matnlaridan beshta madaniy yoki tarixiy ishora toping. Har biri uchun gapni yozing, manbasini ayting, asl voqeani bir gap bilan tushuntiring va bu kontekstdagi ma’nosini yozing. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: kamida to‘rttasida manba va ma’no to‘g‘ri, bittasi o‘zgartirilgan ishora bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda so‘z yasashni, ya’ni old va oxirgi qo‘shimchalarni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: haqiqiy matnlardan beshta madaniy ishorani topib tushuntirish. Keyingi safar old va oxirgi qo‘shimchalar bilan so‘z yasashni o‘rganamiz.

homework_uz: Haqiqiy ingliz matnlaridan (gazeta maqolasi, sarlavha, sharh, podkast yoki serial) beshta madaniy yoki tarixiy ishora toping. Har biri uchun: ishora qilingan gapni yozing, manbasini ayting (mif, Injil, tarix, adabiyot yoki media), asl voqeani bir gap bilan tushuntiring va bu kontekstda nimani anglatishini yozing. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: beshta ishoraning kamida to‘rttasida manba va ma’no to‘g‘ri bo‘lsin, kamida bittasi o‘zgartirilgan ishora (masalan, sarlavhadagi so‘z o‘yini) bo‘lsin.

quiz.q: ‘Spelling is his Achilles’ heel.’ What does this mean?
options: He hurt his foot while writing.
He spells names of heroes well.
quiz.why_uz: Achilles’ heel — yagona zaif nuqta, Axillesning tovonidan.

quiz.q: Which task never ends and achieves nothing?
quiz.why_uz: Sizif toshi har safar pastga qaytadi; Herculean og‘ir, lekin tugaydigan ish.

options: a win that costs almost as much as a defeat
quiz.why_uz: Pirr g‘alabasi juda qimmatga tushgan g‘alaba; ko‘pchilik buni buyuk g‘alaba deb adashadi.

quiz.q: Which phrase means taking an irreversible step?
quiz.why_uz: Sezar Rubikonni kesib o‘tgach, ortga yo‘l qolmagan.

quiz.q: Where does the suffix ‘-gate’ (e.g. Partygate) come from?
In Mary Shelley’s novel, who is Frankenstein?
options: The scientist who creates the monster
quiz.why_uz: Frankenstein — olim; maxluq Frankenstein’s monster deb ataladi.

quiz.q: ‘You need experience to get a job and a job to get experience.’ This is …
quiz.why_uz: Ikki shart bir-biriga bog‘liq, aylanma vaziyat — Catch-22.
Oruellning 1984 romanidan: totalitar nazorat va kuzatuv.

options: He has the touch of a Midas.
quiz.why_uz: The Midas touch qotib qolgan ibora, the bilan keladi.
